seo.shortDescription: Searchable duty table for all 168 HTS Chapter 32 lines — dyes, pigments, titanium dioxide, paints, varnishes, caulk, artists' colors and printing ink. Base rates Free to 6.5%, plus the 2026 Section 301 tariffs (China +37.5%), Canada's 50% Section 338 duty and USMCA.

overview.intro:
Chapter 32 covers coloring products and coatings: tanning extracts (3201–3202), natural and synthetic dyes and pigments (3203–3206), ceramic glazes and glass frit (3207), paints and varnishes (3208–3210), driers, pigment dispersions and stamping foils (3211–3212), artists' colors (3213), caulk, putty and mastics (3214) and inks (3215). Its **168 tariff lines** carry base rates from **Free to 6.5%**, and the U.S. imported **$5.01B** of them in 2025 — most from Canada, Germany, India, Japan and Mexico.

Since **July 24, 2026** the 2026 Section 301 tariffs add 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies, or set a 10% / 12.5% floor for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan; **titanium dioxide pigments** and crude copper phthalocyanine are exempt. Chinese goods also pay the 2018–2019 List 3 duty, **+37.5% in all on most lines**. USMCA-qualifying goods from Canada and Mexico are Free, except that three Canadian subheadings — other solvent-based paints (3208.90), mastics (3214.90.50) and colored printing ink (3215.19.90) — pay a **50% Section 338 duty** from August 22, 2026, USMCA or not. An antidumping order on optical brighteners from China and Taiwan (3204.20.80) is not included in the rates shown.

productGroups.label: Tanning extracts & tannins
productGroups.blurb: Quebracho, wattle, chestnut and other vegetable tanning extracts and tannic acid: 5 lines, Free to 3.1%. Used to tan leather.

productGroups.label: Synthetic tanning agents
productGroups.blurb: Synthetic organic and inorganic tanning substances, tanning preparations and enzymatic pre-tanning preparations: 4 lines, Free to 6.5%.

productGroups.label: Natural colorants (plant & animal)
productGroups.blurb: Annatto, cochineal, logwood, marigold meal and other coloring matter of vegetable or animal origin: 3 lines, Free or 3.1%. Colorants used in food, drugs or cosmetics must also meet FDA's color additive rules.

productGroups.label: Synthetic organic dyes & pigments
productGroups.blurb: Disperse, acid, basic, direct, vat, reactive and solvent dyes, organic pigments such as phthalocyanine blue, FD&C food colors, carotenoids and optical brighteners: 89 lines, mostly 6.5%. Optical brighteners from China and Taiwan also pay antidumping duties.

productGroups.label: Color lakes
productGroups.blurb: Color lakes and preparations based on them, including food coloring solutions with cochineal carmine lake: 11 lines, Free or 6.5%.

productGroups.label: Titanium dioxide & other pigments
productGroups.blurb: Titanium dioxide pigments (3206.11, 80% or more TiO2), chrome, cadmium, iron-oxide, ultramarine and zinc pigments, carbon-black preparations, color masterbatches and luminophores: 16 lines, Free to 6.5%. TiO2 pigments are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 tariffs.

productGroups.label: Ceramic colors, glazes & glass frit
productGroups.blurb: Prepared pigments and opacifiers for ceramics, vitrifiable enamels and glazes, engobes, liquid lustres and glass frit: 5 lines, 3.1% to 6.5%.

productGroups.label: Solvent-based paints & varnishes
productGroups.blurb: Paints, enamels, lacquers and varnishes based on polyesters, acrylic/vinyl or other polymers in a non-aqueous medium (including solvent-based polymer solutions): 3 lines, 3.2% to 3.7%. Canadian 3208.90 pays the 50% Section 338 duty.

productGroups.label: Water-based paints & varnishes
productGroups.blurb: Latex and other water-based paints and varnishes on acrylic/vinyl or other polymers: 2 lines, 5.1% and 5.9%.

productGroups.label: Other paints, distempers & leather finishes
productGroups.blurb: Other paints and varnishes (including enamels, lacquers and distempers) and prepared water pigments for finishing leather: 1 line, 1.8%.

productGroups.label: Paint driers
productGroups.blurb: Prepared driers that speed the curing of oil-based paints: 1 line, 3.7%.

productGroups.label: Pigment dispersions, stamping foils & retail dyes
productGroups.blurb: Pigments (including metallic aluminum pigments) dispersed in non-aqueous media for paint making, hot stamping foils, and dyes put up for retail sale: 3 lines, 3.1% or 4.7%.

productGroups.label: Artists' & students' colors
productGroups.blurb: Artists', students' and signboard painters' colors in tubes, jars, bottles or pans: 6.5% on the entire set for color sets, 3.4% for other colors. China is the largest supplier.

productGroups.label: Caulk, putty, mastics & fillers
productGroups.blurb: Glazier's and grafting putty, resin cements, caulking compounds, other mastics and painters' fillings (3214.10), and non-refractory surfacing preparations for walls and floors (3214.90): 5 lines, Free to 3.7%.

productGroups.label: Printing, writing & drawing inks
productGroups.blurb: Black and colored printing inks (news, flexographic, gravure, letterpress, offset), solid inks shaped for printers, and writing, drawing and other inks: 18 lines, Free to 3.1%. Japan is the largest supplier.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Note 1.** This chapter does not cover: (a) separate chemically defined elements or compounds (except those of heading 3203 or 3204, inorganic products of a kind used as luminophores (heading 3206), glass obtained from fused quartz or other fused silica in the forms provided for in heading 3207, and also dyes and other coloring matter put up in forms or packings for retail sale, of heading 3212); (b) tannates or other tannin derivatives of products of headings 2936 to 2939, 2941 or 3501 to 3504; or (c) mastics of asphalt or other bituminous mastics (heading 2715).

**Note 2.** Heading 3204 includes mixtures of stabilized diazonium salts and couplers for the production of azo dyes.

**Note 3.** Headings 3203, 3204, 3205 and 3206 apply also to preparations based on coloring matter (including, in the case of heading 3206, coloring pigments of heading 2530 or chapter 28, metal flakes and metal powders), of a kind used for coloring any material or used as ingredients in the manufacture of coloring preparations. The headings do not apply, however, to pigments dispersed in nonaqueous media, in liquid or paste form, of a kind used in the manufacture of paints, including enamels (heading 3212), or to other preparations of heading 3207, 3208, 3209, 3210, 3212, 3213 or 3215.

**Note 4.** Heading 3208 includes solutions (other than collodions) consisting of any of the products specified in headings 3901 to 3913 in volatile organic solvents when the weight of the solvent exceeds 50 percent of the weight of the solution.

**Note 5.** The expression "coloring matter" in this chapter does not include products of a kind used as extenders in oil paints, whether or not they are also suitable for coloring distempers.

**Note 6.** The expression "stamping foils" in heading 3212 applies only to thin sheets of a kind used for printing, for example, book covers or hat bands, and consisting of — (a) metallic powder (including powder of precious metal) or pigment, agglomerated with glue, gelatin or other binder; or (b) metal (including precious metal) or pigment, deposited on a supporting sheet of any material.

A tolerance of plus or minus two percentage points from the named percentages is allowable.

seo.shortDescription: What changed for dye, pigment, paint and ink imports since January 2025: the IEEPA duties and their end, the 2026 Section 301 tariffs and TiO2 exemption, Canada's 50% Section 338 duty, the aluminum duty on paints, and the AD orders on optical brighteners and CVP-23.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule: the **2025 Basic Edition**, in force at the start of 2025, and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026). All 168 Chapter 32 lines have the same base rates in both — Free to 6.5%.

What changed were the extra duties. In 2025 the IEEPA duties hit almost every supplier — up to 170% on top of the base rate for Chinese goods in April–May 2025 — and from August 18, 2025 paints, varnishes, artists' colors and mastics also paid the Section 232 aluminum duty on their aluminum content. The IEEPA duties **ended on February 24, 2026**, the Section 232 duty on these goods on **April 6, 2026**, and the Section 122 surcharge that followed expired on **July 23, 2026**. Since **July 24, 2026** the **2026 Section 301 tariffs** apply to 60 economies (titanium dioxide pigments exempt), China still pays its 2018–2019 List 3 duty, and since **August 22, 2026** three Canadian subheadings pay a **50% Section 338 duty**.

Separately, the **antidumping orders** on stilbenic optical brighteners from China and Taiwan remain in force, and the orders on carbazole violet pigment 23 were revoked from June 15, 2026. Antidumping duties are set company by company by the Commerce Department, are listed below for reference, and are **not included in the tariff calculator**.

For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.exemption: Taiwan's rate is a floor: goods pay 10% in total in place of a lower base rate (U.S. note 52(k)). Three subheadings are exempt for every country (U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86): titanium dioxide pigments 3206.11 and 3206.19 and crude copper phthalocyanine 3204.17.20. Five colorant subheadings (3203.00.80, 3204.13.60, 3204.13.80, 3204.18 carotenoids and 3204.90) are exempt only when the goods are for use in pharmaceutical applications (note 52(e), 9903.05.89). The 2025 IEEPA reciprocal duty on Taiwan ended February 24, 2026. Stilbenic optical brighteners (3204.20.80) from Taiwan also pay an antidumping cash deposit (7.61% for Teh Fong Min, 6.19% all others), not shown.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Taiwanese pigment dispersions, paints and inks pay 10% of value in total: $50,000 of aluminum paste pigment (3212.90, 3.1%) pays $5,000.

inEffect.exemption: Switzerland's rate is a floor: goods pay 12.5% in total in place of a lower base rate (U.S. note 52(k)). Three subheadings are exempt for every country (U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86): titanium dioxide pigments 3206.11 and 3206.19 and crude copper phthalocyanine 3204.17.20. Five colorant subheadings (3203.00.80, 3204.13.60, 3204.13.80, 3204.18 carotenoids and 3204.90) are exempt only when the goods are for use in pharmaceutical applications (note 52(e), 9903.05.89). The 2025 IEEPA reciprocal duty on Switzerland ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Swiss dyes and ceramic colors pay 12.5% of value: $100,000 of Swiss pigments pays $12,500.

inEffect.exemption: The 25% Brazil duty (9903.05.01) and the 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.27) stack. Titanium dioxide pigments (3206.11, 3206.19) and crude copper phthalocyanine (3204.17.20) are exempt from both (U.S. notes 50(a)(ii) and 52(b)); the five pharmaceutical-use colorant subheadings are exempt from both when for pharmaceutical use (notes 50(a)(v) and 52(e)). The 2025 IEEPA duties on Brazil (10% plus 40% from August 6, 2025) ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Brazilian tanning agents, paints and dyes pay the base rate plus 37.5%: $50,000 of synthetic tanning agents (3202.10, 6.5%) pays $22,000.

inEffect.measure: Column 2 rates, 35% rate (U.S. note 30), 2026 Section 301 and Section 232 aluminum (Russia)
inEffect.exemption: Russia pays Column 2 rates (general note 3(b)); quebracho extract (3201.10), water-based acrylic paint (3209.10), rubber-based mastics (3214.90.10) and other inks (3215.90.50) pay 35% instead (U.S. note 30(b), 9903.90.08). The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.66) is added except on the note 52(b) subheadings. The 200% Section 232 aluminum duty (9903.85.68) covers 3208.10, 3208.20, 3208.90, 3209.10, 3209.90, 3213.90 and 3214.10, and applies to those goods from any country when their primary aluminum was smelted or cast in Russia (U.S. note 19(m)). The U.S. imported no Chapter 32 goods from Russia in 2025.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian paint is effectively priced out: water-based acrylic paint (3209.10) would pay 35% + 12.5% + 200% = 247.5% of value.

inEffect.exemption: Each listed economy pays +10% or +12.5% on top of the base rate (U.S. note 52), e.g. +12.5% for Israel, Peru, Vietnam, Thailand, Türkiye and Australia, +10% for Malaysia and Indonesia. Three subheadings are exempt for every country (U.S. note 52(b), 9903.05.86): titanium dioxide pigments 3206.11 and 3206.19 and crude copper phthalocyanine 3204.17.20. Five colorant subheadings (3203.00.80, 3204.13.60, 3204.13.80, 3204.18 carotenoids and 3204.90) are exempt only when the goods are for use in pharmaceutical applications (note 52(e), 9903.05.89). An FTA claim (Israel, Peru, Australia …) removes the base rate but not the Section 301 duty (note 52(a)). The 2025 IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Israeli printing ink (1.8%) pays 14.3%; Peruvian cochineal-based colorants (3203.00.10, Free) pay 12.5%; Vietnamese artists' colors pay 15.9% (3213.90) or 19% (sets).

changes.title: No Chapter 32 base-rate changes
changes.detail: All 168 Chapter 32 tariff lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition; no line was added, removed or renumbered. The temporary duty suspensions for specific dyes, pigments and paints in Chapter 99 subchapter II (9902.xx) expired on December 31, 2020 and have not been renewed.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29), with no Chapter 32 exemption. The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: China Section 301 duties continue during the four-year review
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018 China actions, so they did not terminate on their July 6 and August 23, 2026 anniversaries and remain in effect pending the statutory review. The 25% List 3 duty on Chinese dyes, pigments, paints and inks continues.

changes.title: 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian paints, mastics and printing inks
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 (signed July 20, 2026, in response to Canada's surtax on U.S. motor vehicles) imposed 50% on a list of Canadian products (U.S. note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14) that includes other solvent-based paints and varnishes (3208.90.00), other mastics and surfacing preparations (3214.90.50) and colored printing inks (3215.19.90). The duty applies even to USMCA-qualifying goods, on top of the 10% Section 301 duty for non-USMCA goods. Proclamation 11056 moved the start from August 19 to August 22, 2026.

changes.title: Carbazole violet pigment 23 orders revoked
changes.detail: No U.S. producer took part in the fourth five-year reviews, so Commerce revoked the 2004 antidumping orders on carbazole violet pigment 23 (3204.17.90.40) from China and India and the countervailing duty order on India, effective for entries from June 15, 2026. The ITC terminated its reviews on August 14, 2026.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies take effect
changes.detail: +10% or +12.5% on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84), or a 10% / 12.5% floor for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan. 165 of the 168 Chapter 32 lines are covered; titanium dioxide pigments (3206.11, 3206.19) and crude copper phthalocyanine (3204.17.20) are on the note 52(b) exemption list, and five colorant subheadings are exempt for pharmaceutical use (note 52(e)). USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt.

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 150-day 10% surcharge on goods of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026, the day before the 2026 Section 301 tariffs began.

changes.title: Brazil Section 301 tariff takes effect
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) on 165 of the 168 Chapter 32 lines; the same three subheadings as in note 52(b) are exempt (U.S. note 50(a)(ii)). From July 24 the 12.5% 2026 duty is added, for +37.5% in total.

changes.title: Optical brighteners from Taiwan: 1.96% preliminary margin
changes.detail: In the 2024–2025 administrative review, Commerce preliminarily found a 1.96% dumping margin for Teh Fong Min. The 7.61% cash deposit stays in force until the final results.

changes.title: USMCA joint review: not renewed, still in force
changes.detail: The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. USTR said the Agreement remains in force pending resolution of the issues or until termination, so USMCA claims (SPI S) still apply.

changes.title: Optical brighteners from Taiwan: 7.61% cash deposit
changes.detail: Final results of the 2023–2024 administrative review of the antidumping order on stilbenic optical brighteners from Taiwan: 7.61% for Teh Fong Min, collected as a cash deposit on later entries; 6.19% for all other exporters.

changes.title: Section 232 aluminum duty on paints and mastics ends
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 replaced the aluminum derivative headings (9903.85.01–9903.85.15 terminated) with a new metals list (U.S. note 16, 9903.82.xx) that includes no Chapter 32 line. Paints, varnishes, artists' colors and mastics no longer pay a Section 232 duty, except the 200% on Russian aluminum (9903.85.68).

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge replaces the IEEPA tariffs
changes.detail: A 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) applied until July 23, 2026. Six Chapter 32 subheadings were on its product exemption list (9903.03.03): 3203.00.80, 3204.13.80, 3204.17.20, 3204.18.00, 3206.11.00 and 3206.19.00. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico were exempt (9903.03.07, 9903.03.08).

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China, Brazil, India and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them for goods entered from 12:00 a.m. ET on February 24.

changes.title: India's extra 25% IEEPA duty removed
changes.detail: Executive Order 14384 ended the additional 25% duty on products of India (9903.01.84) from February 7, 2026. India's 25% reciprocal rate ended with the other IEEPA duties on February 24.

changes.title: China IEEPA duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong (9903.01.24) fell from +20% to +10%, on top of the 10% reciprocal duty and the 25% List 3 duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Extra 25% duty on products of India
changes.detail: Executive Order 14329 added 25% on Indian goods (9903.01.84) over India's purchases of Russian oil, on top of the 25% reciprocal rate: Indian dyes at a 6.5% base rate paid 56.5%. Removed February 7, 2026.

changes.title: Paints, varnishes and mastics added to the Section 232 aluminum derivative list
changes.detail: Commerce added 3208.10, 3208.20, 3208.90, 3209.10, 3209.90, 3213.90 and 3214.10 to the aluminum derivative list (U.S. note 19(k)). From August 18, 2025 these goods paid the 50% aluminum duty on the value of their aluminum content (9903.85.08), and Russian goods 200% (9903.85.68). The all-country duty ended April 6, 2026; the Russian 200% remains.

changes.title: Country-specific reciprocal rates replace the 10% baseline
changes.detail: Executive Order 14326 set each country's reciprocal rate (9903.02.xx), for example 25% for India and 15% for the EU including the base rate. Six Chapter 32 subheadings are on the reciprocal-tariff exemption list (U.S. note 2(v)(iii)(a), 9903.01.32): 3203.00.80, 3204.13.80, 3204.17.20, 3204.18.00, 3206.11.00 and 3206.19.00. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: 40% IEEPA duty on products of Brazil
changes.detail: Executive Order 14323 (signed July 30, 2025) added 40% on goods of Brazil on top of the 10% reciprocal duty. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Canada IEEPA duty raised to 35%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on non-USMCA Canadian goods (9903.01.10) rose from 25% to 35%. USMCA goods stayed exempt. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty cut from 125% to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14298 cut the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 10%. Chinese pigments and paints then paid 10% + 20% (fentanyl) + 25% (List 3) on top of the base rate. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China reciprocal duty raised to 125%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14266 raised the reciprocal duty on Chinese goods to 125%. With the 20% fentanyl duty and the 25% List 3 duty, most Chinese Chapter 32 goods paid 170% on top of the base rate until May 13, 2025.

changes.title: 10% reciprocal tariff on most Chapter 32 goods
changes.detail: A 10% baseline duty (9903.01.25) on products of all countries except Canada and Mexico, signed April 2, 2025 (Executive Order 14257). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Optical brightener antidumping orders continued
changes.detail: After the Court of International Trade set aside their 2022 revocation (orders reinstated June 2024) and the second five-year reviews, Commerce continued the 2012 antidumping orders on stilbenic optical brighteners from China and Taiwan (classified in 3204.20.80), effective February 27, 2025. The China-wide rate set in the 2012 order is 106.17%.

changes.title: USMCA goods exempted from the Canada and Mexico duties
changes.detail: Goods entered under USMCA were exempted from the 25% IEEPA duties on Canada and Mexico. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China IEEPA duty raised to 20%
changes.detail: The IEEPA duty on products of China and Hong Kong went from +10% (from February 4, 2025) to +20%, on top of the Section 301 lists.

changes.title: Additional duties on products of Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +25% on goods of Canada (9903.01.10) and Mexico (9903.01.01), in force from March 4, 2025, including paints, pigments and inks. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: List 4A duty on Chinese vat dyes cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: The List 4A duty (9903.88.15) on synthetic indigo (3204.15.10) and other vat dyes (3204.15.80) from China fell from 15% to 7.5%.

changes.title: List 3 duty on Chinese Chapter 32 goods raised to 25%
changes.detail: The List 3 duty (9903.88.03), in force at 10% since September 24, 2018, rose to 25%. It covers 163 of the 168 Chapter 32 lines.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 32 goods were **$5.01B in 2025**, down 6.1% from $5.33B in 2024 and below the 2022 peak of $5.91B. The largest products are titanium dioxide pigments ($510M, 3206.11, down 15.9%), caulking compounds, mastics and painters' fillings ($483M, 3214.10), colored printing inks ($448M, 3215.19), organic pigments ($418M, 3204.17) and other solvent-based paints ($384M, 3208.90).

**Canada** ($977M, 19.5%) is the largest supplier: $363M of other coloring matter (heading 3206, which includes TiO2 pigments), $358M of paints and varnishes (3208–3209) and $119M of mastics. **Germany** ($644M) ships paints, dyes, pigments and mastics; **India** ($387M) is the main source of synthetic dyes ($254M of heading 3204) and natural colorants ($64M); **Japan** ($386M) led by printing ink ($173M); **Mexico** ($366M) paints, pigments, mastics and ceramic glazes. **China** ($293M) supplies pigments, dyes and artists' colors (largest supplier of heading 3213, $52M); its share fell from 9.5% in 2020 to 5.8% in 2025, a period in which Chinese goods paid the 25% List 3 duty.

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data, so the 2026 Section 301 and Section 338 duties are not yet reflected. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 32: Dyes, Pigments, Paints & Inks — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Paint, Pigments, Dyes & Ink: Rules and Legal Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 32) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 32 line — TSCA certification, FDA color additives, CPSC lead-paint limit, EPA VOC rules, art material labeling, hazmat shipping, the optical-brightener antidumping order — and the legal ways to pay less: USMCA, FTAs, pharmaceutical use, drawback, FTZ, first sale.

tariffEngineering.intro:
What a Chapter 32 import costs depends mostly on **origin**: USMCA goods from Canada and Mexico are Free (except three Canadian lines at 50%), the EU pays 10% in total, Japan and Korea 12.5%, India and the UK the base rate plus 10%, and China the base rate plus 37.5%. The legal ways to pay less are claiming USMCA or another FTA, declaring pharmaceutical use for certain colorants, drawback on exported goods and a correct customs value.

The paperwork depends on the product: every dye, pigment, paint and ink needs a **TSCA** certification, colors for food, drugs and cosmetics must meet **FDA** color-additive rules, consumer paints the **CPSC** lead limit, architectural and spray paints **EPA** VOC limits, artists' colors the art-material labeling rule, and flammable paints and inks the **DOT** hazmat rules. Each rule and lever below links to its regulation.

levers.title: Claim USMCA for Canadian and Mexican goods
levers.saves: The base rate (up to 6.5%) and the 10% Section 301 duty on goods of Canada (9903.05.29) or Mexico (9903.05.55)
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer; it need not follow a prescribed format and CBP can ask for it.
levers.caveat: The 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian 3208.90, 3214.90.50 and 3215.19.90 applies even with a USMCA claim. The USMCA was not renewed at the July 1, 2026 joint review but remains in force.

citations.label: USTR statement on the USMCA joint review (July 1, 2026)

levers.title: Claim the FTA rate for other partner countries
levers.saves: The base rate (1.5%–6.5%) for goods of Israel, Peru, Chile, Colombia, Australia, Singapore and the other FTA partners listed in the Special column
levers.document: Proof of origin under the agreement (certificate or importer's knowledge, as the agreement requires), claimed with its SPI code.
levers.caveat: An FTA claim does not remove the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(a)); for Korea, the 12.5% floor applies whatever the KORUS rate. GSP (A, A+) has been expired since December 31, 2020.

levers.title: Declare pharmaceutical use for qualifying colorants
levers.saves: The 10%–12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty (and Brazil's 25%) on colorants used in pharmaceutical applications
levers.document: Entry under heading 9903.05.89 (Brazil: 9903.05.06), with records showing the goods are for use in pharmaceutical applications.
levers.caveat: Only for the pharmaceutical end use; the same colorants for food or industrial use pay the duty. China's 25% List 3 duty still applies.

levers.title: Know the country of origin — China pays 37.5% extra
levers.saves: Up to 27.5 points: most Chinese Chapter 32 goods pay +37.5%, the same goods from India or the UK +10%, from the EU 10% in total
levers.document: Production records showing where the dye, pigment or paint was made. Mere dilution or simple repacking abroad does not change origin under the 19 CFR part 102 rules (19 CFR 102.17); for other cases ask CBP for a binding ruling.
levers.caveat: Antidumping orders follow their own scope and country rules. Goods made with Russian-smelted aluminum pay 200% on 7 subheadings whatever the origin.

levers.title: Check the optical-brightener antidumping scope before you buy
levers.saves: The whole antidumping deposit (China-wide 106.17%), when the product is outside the order
levers.appliesTo: 3204.20.80 (fluorescent brightening agents), from China and Taiwan
levers.document: The order's written scope covers triazinylaminostilbenes; it, not the HTS number, decides. When unsure, request a scope ruling from Commerce.
levers.caveat: Covered goods pay the deposit even when entered under another HTS number (the orders also list 2933.69, 2921.59).

levers.title: Declare the right transaction value
levers.saves: Duty on the part of the price that is not dutiable value, for every ad valorem duty on the entry
levers.appliesTo: All dutiable lines and every country with a Section 301 or 338 duty
levers.document: Invoices and contracts showing the sale for exportation to the United States; in a multi-tier chain, an earlier sale can be the basis when it was a bona fide sale for export to the U.S.
levers.caveat: CBP can reject a value that is not supported by the sale documents.

levers.title: Claim drawback on exported goods
levers.saves: Up to 99% of the duties paid on imported dyes, pigments or paints that are re-exported or used to make exported products
levers.document: A drawback claim to CBP with import and export records (19 CFR part 191).
levers.caveat: Antidumping and countervailing duties cannot be refunded as drawback (19 CFR 191.3).

levers.title: Use a foreign-trade zone to defer or avoid duty on re-exports
levers.saves: Duty is paid only when goods leave the zone for U.S. consumption; none on goods exported from the zone
levers.caveat: Goods subject to the 2026 Section 301 duties must be admitted in privileged foreign status, so making paint in a zone does not avoid the Section 301 duty on its foreign inputs.

levers.title: Enter returned U.S. goods under Chapter 98
levers.saves: The full duty, including the 2026 Section 301 duty, on U.S.-made pigments, paints or inks returned without being advanced in value
levers.appliesTo: All 168 lines, for products of the United States
levers.document: Declaration and export records required for American goods returned (19 CFR 10.1).
levers.caveat: Goods processed abroad do not qualify under 9801.00.10; 9802 provisions pay duty on the foreign processing value.

provisions.text: Products of the United States returned without having been advanced in value or improved in condition abroad

rules.title: TSCA import certification (positive or negative) for every chemical substance or mixture: dyes, pigments, paints, inks and mastics
Color additives for food, drugs, cosmetics or medical devices must be FDA-listed (e.g. FD&C Red No. 40, titanium dioxide, annatto, carmine), and FD&C colors need FDA batch certification
Paint and similar surface coatings for consumer use may not contain more than 0.009% lead (90 ppm); artists' paints are exempt
Architectural coatings: importers must meet the national VOC content limits and label each container with the manufacture date and the other required information
Aerosol coatings (spray paint): reactivity-based VOC limits for regulated entities, including importers
Art materials (artists' colors, drawing inks): chronic-hazard review and labeling under ASTM D-4236
Flammable paints, printing inks, driers and pigment dispersions in solvent are hazardous materials for shipping papers, marking and packaging
Stilbenic optical brighteners from China (China-wide 106.17%) and Taiwan (Teh Fong Min 7.61%, others 6.19%): antidumping cash deposit (not in the tariff calculator)
200% Section 232 duty when the product is Russian or its primary aluminum was smelted or cast in Russia (paints, varnishes, artists' colors and mastics on the aluminum derivative list)

groups.note: Colorants sold for food, drug, cosmetic or medical-device use must be FDA-listed color additives (21 CFR parts 70–74). Other colorants (3203.00.80) used in pharmaceutical applications can skip the 2026 Section 301 duty (U.S. note 52(e)).

groups.note: Titanium dioxide pigments (3206.11, 3206.19) are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (U.S. note 52(b)) and pay only their 6% base rate, plus 25% if Chinese. Titanium dioxide itself, not prepared as a pigment, is 2823.00.00 (5.5%) in Chapter 28.

Flammable paint is a hazardous material in transport. Canadian 3208.90 pays the 50% Section 338 duty, USMCA or not.

keyTakeaways: Chapter 32 base rates run from Free to 6.5%. Since July 24, 2026 the 2026 Section 301 tariffs add 10% or 12.5% for 60 economies, or set a 10% total for the EU and Taiwan and 12.5% for Japan, Korea and Switzerland.
China pays the base rate plus 37.5% on most lines (25% List 3 + 12.5%). Titanium dioxide pigments are exempt from the 2026 duties for every country.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on paint imported into the U.S.?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on paint
faqs.answer: Yes. Paints and varnishes have base rates of 3.2%–3.7% (solvent-based, 3208), 5.1%–5.9% (water-based, 3209) and 1.8% (other, 3210). Since July 24, 2026 the 2026 Section 301 tariffs apply: German and other EU paint pays 10% in total, Japanese and Korean 12.5%, British and Indian the base rate plus 10%, Chinese the base rate plus 37.5%. USMCA paint from Mexico is Free; from Canada it is Free except 3208.90, which pays 50% under Section 338.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on paint from China?
faqs.answer: The base rate plus 37.5%: 25% under Section 301 List 3 and 12.5% under the 2026 Section 301 action. Solvent-based paint (3208) pays 40.7%–41.2%, water-based paint (3209) 42.6%–43.4%, and artists' acrylic colors (3213) 40.9%, or 44% for sets. Consumer paint must also meet the 0.009% lead limit (16 CFR part 1303), and spray paint the EPA aerosol-coating VOC rules.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for paint?
searchedAs: hs code for paints and varnishes
faqs.answer: Paints and varnishes are headings 3208–3210. Solvent-based paints are 3208: 3208.10 polyester, 3208.20 acrylic or vinyl, 3208.90 others such as epoxy and polyurethane (3.2%–3.7%). Water-based (latex) paints are 3209: 3209.10 acrylic or vinyl (5.1%), 3209.90 others (5.9%). Other paints, distempers and leather finishes are 3210.00 (1.8%). Artists' paints are 3213, and paint thinners and removers are classified outside Chapter 32.

faqs.question: What is the HS code and tariff for titanium dioxide?
searchedAs: hs code for titanium dioxide pigment
hs code for titanium dioxide rutile
faqs.answer: Titanium dioxide pigments with 80% or more TiO2 are 3206.11.00; other TiO2-based pigments and preparations are 3206.19.00. Both pay 6% and are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so they pay no extra duty from the EU, Japan, India or other countries; USMCA pigment from Canada is Free, and Chinese pigment pays 31% (6% + 25% List 3). Titanium oxide not prepared as a pigment is 2823.00.00 (5.5%).

faqs.question: Is there a U.S. antidumping duty on titanium dioxide from China?
searchedAs: anti dumping duty on titanium dioxide from china
faqs.answer: No. No U.S. antidumping or countervailing duty order on titanium dioxide pigment is in force. Chinese TiO2 pigment pays the 6% base rate and the 25% Section 301 List 3 duty, 31% in all. The Chapter 32 antidumping order in force covers stilbenic optical brighteners (3204.20.80) from China and Taiwan.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for pigments?
searchedAs: hs code for iron oxide pigment
hs code for carbon black pigment
faqs.answer: Organic pigments are 3204.17 (6.5% for most, with named pigments such as pigment blue 15:3 or pigment red 122 in their own lines). Inorganic pigments are in 3206: titanium dioxide 3206.11/.19 (6%), chrome pigments 3206.20 (3.7%), ultramarine 3206.41 (1.5%), iron oxide preparations 3206.49.20 (6.5%), carbon black preparations 3206.49.40 (Free), concentrated dispersions in plastics 3206.49.10 (5.9%). Pigments dispersed in non-aqueous media for paint making are 3212.90 (3.1%). Plain iron oxides (2821.10) and carbon black (2803.00) are in Chapter 28.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for dyes?
faqs.answer: Synthetic dyes are heading 3204: disperse 3204.11, acid 3204.12, basic 3204.13, direct 3204.14, vat 3204.15, reactive 3204.16, solvent and other dyes 3204.19 — mostly 6.5%. Natural dyes of plant or animal origin are 3203 (Free or 3.1%); dyes put up for retail sale are 3212.90 (3.1%); hair dyes are cosmetics in Chapter 33. Indian dyes pay 16.5% in total, Chinese dyes 44%.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for food coloring?
searchedAs: hs code for synthetic food colours
faqs.answer: Synthetic food colors are in 3204.12.50, with their own lines for FD&C Red 40, Yellow 5 and Yellow 6 (6.5%); carotenoids are 3204.18 (3.1%). Natural colors such as annatto and cochineal are 3203.00.10 (Free); color lakes and food coloring solutions with carmine lake are 3205. FD&C colors must come from FDA-certified batches for use in food (21 CFR part 80).

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on dyes and pigments from China and India?
faqs.answer: For Chapter 32 goods, China pays the base rate plus 37.5% (25% List 3 + 12.5% 2026 Section 301), so most dyes and pigments pay 44%. India pays the base rate plus 10%, 16.5% on most dyes. In 2025 IEEPA duties reached 50% extra on Indian goods (August 27, 2025 to February 7, 2026) and 145% on Chinese goods (April 10 to May 13, 2025, plus List 3); all IEEPA duties ended February 24, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for printing ink?
searchedAs: hs code for offset printing ink
hs tariff code for printer ink
faqs.answer: Printing ink is 3215.11 (black) and 3215.19 (other colors), with statistical lines for news, flexographic, gravure, letterpress and offset ink (1.8%). Solid ink in engineered shapes for printers of heading 8443 is 3215.11.10 or 3215.19.10 (Free). Writing, drawing and other inks are 3215.90 (drawing ink 3.1%, others 1.8%).

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on printer ink?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most ink lines have a 1.8% base rate. Japanese ink pays 12.5% in total, German 10%, British 11.8%, Israeli 14.3% and Chinese 39.3%. USMCA ink from Mexico and Canada is Free, except Canadian colored printing ink of 3215.19.90, which pays 50% under Section 338 from August 22, 2026.

faqs.question: Are there tariffs on art supplies like paints?
searchedAs: are there tariffs on art supplies
faqs.answer: Artists' and students' colors are 3213: 6.5% on the entire set for color sets, 3.4% for other colors. From China they pay 44% and 40.9%, from Vietnam 19% and 15.9%, from France or other EU countries 10%. Art materials must carry ASTM D-4236 chronic-hazard labeling (16 CFR 1500.14(b)(8)). Brushes and canvas are classified in other chapters.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for caulk, sealant and putty?
faqs.answer: Glazier's putty, resin cements, caulking compounds, other mastics and painters' fillings are 3214.10 (3.7%), with statistical lines for caulking compounds, other mastics and painters' fillings. Non-refractory surfacing preparations such as wall putty are 3214.90 (rubber-based Free, others 3.25%). Products sold as adhesives are classified in heading 3506.

faqs.question: What does HTS Chapter 32 cover?
faqs.answer: Chapter 32 covers tanning and dyeing extracts, tannins, dyes, pigments and other coloring matter, paints and varnishes, putty and other mastics, and inks: 15 headings (3201–3215) and 168 U.S. tariff lines with base rates from Free to 6.5%. The U.S. imported $5.01B of these goods in 2025.
